target.output: public epoch freshness parity canary and worker preflight drift receipt

problem: Public EPOCH projection can trail live main during a rapid identical-worker wave, while the constitution requires workers to read latest public EPOCH immediately before material writes; without an explicit drift receipt/freshness policy, workers can satisfy the read mechanically yet bind provenance to a stale projected main.
acceptance: A canary proves whether public EPOCH catches up monotonically to live main under rapid worker commits without regressing.
Worker preflight emits both public EPOCH main and exact live main head when they differ, and fails closed for authority decisions that require parity.
Drift is classified as projection lag rather than silently treating either source as equivalent authority.
No Current Human Accepted Served or shared authority promotion occurs.
title: Public EPOCH drift receipt and parity canary
mission: Measure public EPOCH projection lag against exact live main across a controlled rapid-commit window, define a replayable drift receipt consumed by worker preflight, and falsify any policy that mechanically treats a successfully fetched but stale projected main as equivalent to the exact live head. Keep all output candidate-only and do not change authority or promotion semantics.

information_gain.reason: This /wc observed public EPOCH main bc28f0decb7c while live main was already b9582bf0d9cb1a4ff239a7555e05166e192822c0, so the system lacks explicit evidence about how much lag is expected and when parity matters.

regression_prevention.reason: The Global Agent Constitution makes public EPOCH a mandatory prewrite input. A durable drift receipt would prevent a worker from equating successful EPOCH fetch with exact live-head freshness during heavy concurrent commits.

candidate_read_scope: repository publication/runtime scripts and workflows that project EPOCH
recent main commit lineage during the canary window

fail_if: the canary calls parity PASS while projected EPOCH main moves backward or skips a policy-required freshness boundary
worker preflight hides a mismatch between projected EPOCH main and exact live main
the proposal changes Current Human Accepted Served or shared authority semantics
a stale projection is treated as proof that live target bytes were read
falsification.pass_if: Across a controlled rapid-commit window the verifier can reconstruct projected EPOCH versus exact live main, classify lag explicitly, demonstrate monotonic catch-up behavior or surface counterexamples, and emit a bounded preflight drift receipt without authority promotion.
